import re

def parse_ipv4(text):
    # Regular expression to match a valid IPv4 address
    ipv4_pattern = r'^((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\.){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)$'
    
    # Check if the input matches the IPv4 pattern
    if not re.match(ipv4_pattern, text):
        raise ValueError("Invalid IPv4 address")
    
    # Split the input string into parts
    parts = text.split('.')
    
    # Convert each part to an integer and check for leading zeros
    numbers = [int(part) for part in parts if part == '0' or not part.startswith('0')]
    
    # Return the tuple of integers
    return tuple(numbers)

def luhn_valid(number):
    # Remove all spaces from the input string
    number = number.replace(" ", "")
    
    # Check if the length of the string is less than 2
    if len(number) < 2:
        return False
    
    # Initialize the sum of the digits
    total_sum = 0
    
    # Iterate over the string from right to left
    for i, digit in enumerate(reversed(number)):
        if not digit.isdigit():
            return False
        
        # Convert the digit to an integer
        digit = int(digit)
        
        # Double every second digit from the right
        if i % 2 == 1:
            digit *= 2
            if digit > 9:
                digit -= 9
        
        # Add the digit to the total sum
        total_sum += digit
    
    # Check if the total sum is divisible by 10
    return total_sum % 10 == 0

def luhn_valid(number):
    # Remove all spaces from the input string
    number = number.replace(" ", "")
    
    # Check if the resulting string contains only digits
    if not number.isdigit():
        return False
    
    # If the string contains fewer than 2 digits, return False
    if len(number) < 2:
        return False
    
    # Apply the Luhn algorithm
    total = 0
    num_digits = len(number)
    parity = num_digits % 2
    
    for i in range(num_digits):
        digit = int(number[i])
        if i % 2 == parity:
            digit *= 2
            if digit > 9:
                digit -= 9
        total += digit
    
    # Check if the total sum is divisible by 10
    return total % 10 == 0
